newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: El Nino seen trimming Australian wool output.
newsitem.headline: El Nino seen trimming Australian wool output.

text.p: El Nino-inspired drought is likely to have a negative impact on wool production in eastern and southern Australia over the next two seasons, Wool International (WI) said in its monthly Insight newsletter.
This would occur if the El Nino weather pattern continued, but seasonal factors were likely to influence the market over the next six months, WI said.
A lack of feed and water during a drought usually means sheep produce finer wool, but less of it than normal.
The Australian Wool Production Forecasting Committee is due to meet on August 21 to review the shorn wool production estimate for 1996/97 (to June 30) and the forecast for 1997/98.
Current forecasts were for a slight increase in wool production in 1997/98 compared with 1996/97, WI said.

"However, this could change given the recent dry conditions experienced over much of southern and eastern Australia," it said. "The production forecast for 1997/98 could be revised down slightly in comparison to the 1996/97 production estimate."
The Wool Production Forecasting Committee in March forecast Australian shorn wool production would rise by 0.9 percent to 645 million kg in 1997/98, the first increase since 1992/93.
Demand fundamentals continued to gradually improve, although economic indicators were very mixed among the major wool consuming countries, WI said.
A modest pick-up in retail wool demand was anticipated in 1997/98 from the depressed level of 1996/97, it said.
Wool International is the manager of Australia's wool stockpile of 1.5 million bales.
